name: Ampakines (CX717 etc.)

lead: Ampakines are research compounds that amplify glutamate signalling at AMPA receptors. People interested in focus and memory follow them as potential cognitive enhancers.
CX717 showed promise in a 2025 ADHD trial, while CX516 had mixed results in schizophrenia studies. No ampakine is approved.

paras: They slow AMPA channel deactivation so each glutamate signal lasts longer, supporting plasticity and BDNF expression.
Investigational with limited human data; high-impact types carry seizure risk at high doses in preclinical work.

angle.text: Ampakines attract people seeking better focus, memory and alertness for studying, work and training. They remain investigational research compounds.

lead: Ampakines are a class of experimental drugs that strengthen the brain's AMPA glutamate receptors, the receptors responsible for fast excitatory signalling. They are discussed in nootropic and focus communities as memory, alertness and cognition enhancers, which people link to sharper study, work and training performance. The best-known members are CX516, CX717, CX1739 and farampator (Org 24448) [1][2].

They act as positive allosteric modulators: they slow the closing of the AMPA channel after glutamate binds, prolonging the signal without activating the receptor themselves [1][1]. The compounds were developed from the 1990s by Cortex Pharmaceuticals, and none has been approved as a medicine [1][3].

Human studies include CX516 added to antipsychotics in schizophrenia, CX516 in mild cognitive impairment, farampator in healthy elderly volunteers, and a 2025 phase 2a trial of CX717 in adult ADHD [4][5][6][7][8]. CX717 also reversed opioid-induced breathing depression in volunteers in work described in reviews [9][1].

paras: Ampakines bind an allosteric site on AMPA receptors and slow deactivation and desensitisation, lengthening synaptic currents and supporting long-term potentiation [1][1]. Lab work shows they can raise BDNF expression [10][11]. Low-impact types (CX516, CX1739) and high-impact types (CX717, farampator) are distinguished by how strongly they alter receptor kinetics [1][2].

Early human work showed CX516 improved memory encoding in healthy older volunteers [12]. Schizophrenia add-on trials of CX516 reported little cognitive benefit [13][4][14]. CX717 reduced effects of sleep deprivation in monkeys [15] and showed promise in a 2025 adult ADHD trial [7]. CX1739 was tested for safety in healthy young volunteers [16]. Respiratory research examines ampakines for opioid-induced respiratory depression [9].

Registered trials include CX516 with clozapine, olanzapine or risperidone (n=105) [17], CX717 in adult ADHD (n=68) [18], CX516 in fragile X syndrome and autism [19], and CX1739 for opioid respiratory depression [20]. Two depression studies of AMPA modulators were withdrawn or terminated [21][22].
High-impact ampakines are described as having a narrower margin, with seizures reported at high doses in preclinical work [1]. Human safety data are limited to early-phase trials.
